newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat surges, ends higher after funds buy.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat surges, ends higher after funds buy.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures surged to five-month highs in a late rally in which funds bought the May (and July) contract after technical buy stops were hit, traders said.
"Funds are buying the May and the July, and March is just following," a trader said at the close. "It's a break-out."
Traders said E. D. & F. Man International, a brokerage linked to large fund holdings, bought 3.2 million May bushels and two million July.
Refco, another commission house with fund ties, bought 2.3 million May and 1.2 million July.
Traders said it was probably only a matter of time before funds started buying wheat, after having been active buyers of corn throughout the week.

KCBT wheat settled four to 10-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 10-3/4 cents at $4.32-3/4. The last time the March contract closed higher than that level was Sept 10, 1996, when it closed at $4.47-1/4.
May also gained 10-3/4 cents to settle at $4.06-3/4. The last time it closed above that level was Sept 26, when it closed at $4.07.
New crop July, which had been lower early after areas of Kansas reeceived more moisture than expected, also closed higher amid buying by both funds and commercials.
Other players included FIMAT, Benson-Quinn, Cargill Investors Services, Linnco and Prudential, which each bought at least one million May bushels.
